**For most MacBook Airs, a 30W USB-C charger is the minimum, and a 70W one is the choice if you want fast charging.**

**By model (per [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):**
- **2022 or later:** Apple recommends the 30W (13-inch only), 35W Dual USB-C, 67W, or 70W adapter, used with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable.
- **2018-2021:** Apple recommends the 30W USB-C adapter or the 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max.

**What ships in the box:**
- **13-inch M5 (2026):** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max. Apple lists a minimum of 30W to charge and says fast charging needs a 70W or higher USB PD source ([Apple specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/), [M5 tech specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **13-inch M4 (2025):** a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W Dual USB-C Port adapter with the 10-core GPU. Fast charging requires the 70W adapter ([M4 tech specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).

**Practical advice:**
- If you just need a replacement or spare, get 30W-35W or higher. A 35W dual-port model also lets you charge a phone at the same time.
- If you want fast charging, get 70W or higher.
- Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery works, even one with higher or lower wattage than Apple recommends. For the best experience, use at least the wattage Apple recommends for your model ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).
- To see what your current charger delivers, hold Option, click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power. The wattage is under AC Charger Information.
